scope: Independent read-only source review of keyring 3.6.3 Linux feature selection for codex-keyring-store and codex-rmcp-client.
decision: No source-level API or credential-namespace incompatibility identified. Native service behavior is not independently exercised by this review.

findings.detail: Both owners use synchronous Entry::new, get_password, set_password and delete_credential. The API surface does not change with the selected Linux backend feature.

Both persistent feature choices select the same keyutils_persistent default module and constructor. SsCredential maps service to service, account to username, absent target to default, application to rust-keyring and uses the same label. OAuth KEYRING_SERVICE and compute_store_key are unchanged.

The same SsCredential implementation searches service/username/target, falls back to the legacy default-collection search when no target match exists, prefers updating an existing entry, and selects EncryptionType::Dh while crypto-rust is enabled.

In upstream keyring 3.6.3, KeyutilsPersistentCredentialBuilder::build actually constructs SsCredential directly, despite its documentation naming KeyutilsPersistentCredential. Both old and new feature paths share this implementation. DefaultKeyringStore does not override it. A claim that this migration verifies or preserves an active kernel keyring cache is unsupported; the observed default builder is SecretService-only in both configurations.

The conditional import changes from secret_service::blocking to dbus_secret_service. Both expose synchronous methods here. Native error text, timing and environment interaction can differ; source-level API equivalence does not establish identical runtime behavior.

vendored propagates through dbus-secret-service to dbus and libdbus-sys. It vendors the native D-Bus library for builds; it is not evidence that the complete backend is pure Rust or that a SecretService daemon exists.

OAuth unit fixtures use MockKeyringStore. The process store-pinning test child installs TestCredentialBuilder explicitly. These cover credential format, policy and recovery semantics but not a real native SecretService. No gnome-keyring/dbus-run-session setup was found in the inspected workflow/scripts. Native old-entry read/write, unlocking and persistence across reboot were not run in this review.

recommendation: Retain the narrowly scoped feature migration and report source-level API/namespace compatibility. Let actual new-head build/tests establish compilation. Do not describe mock-backed tests as native SecretService verification or assert a kernel cache on the observed default path.
